title: MAO Inhibitors, Atypical Antidepressants, and Serotonin Syndrome

steps.title: MAOI Classification
steps.tx: **Monoamine oxidase inhibitor subclasses** divide into non-selective irreversible blockers (phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid) that destroy both MAO-A and MAO-B enzymes, selective reversible inhibitors of MAO-A known as RIMAs (moclobemide), and selective MAO-B inhibitors like selegiline and rasagiline. MAO-A preferentially metabolizes serotonin and norepinephrine, whereas MAO-B deaminates phenylethylamine and benzylamine.

steps.title: Tyramine Hypertensive Crisis
steps.tx: **Hypertensive crisis cheese reaction** occurs when patients on irreversible MAO inhibitors ingest foods rich in tyramine, such as aged cheeses, draught beer, cured salami, yeast extracts, or broad bean pods. Normally, intestinal and hepatic MAO-A rapidly catabolizes dietary tyramine; when MAO-A is inhibited, intact tyramine enters circulation, displacing massive quantities of norepinephrine into vascular synapses.

steps.title: Serotonin Syndrome Pathogenesis
steps.tx: **Pathophysiology of serotonin syndrome** represents a predictable hyper-serotonergic toxic state provoked by combining serotonergic agents with differing mechanisms, such as an SSRI with an MAOI, tramadol, linezolid, triptans, or Saint John wort. Symptoms typically explode within 6 to 24 hours of medication introduction, driven by excessive stimulation of post-synaptic 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors.

steps.tx: Press on this ankle and the foot keeps beating long after your hand lets go. Sustained and spontaneous **clonus** like this, with tremor, sweating and agitation, separates serotonin syndrome from its mimics at the bedside. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome instead turns muscles lead pipe rigid and slow, so the reflexes themselves arbitrate between the two emergencies. Serotonin toxicity also declares its cause in the drug chart, a recently added serotonergic agent or dose rise within the past day.
steps.say: Inducible and spontaneous ankle clonus with agitation is the bedside hallmark of serotonin syndrome.

steps.title: Serotonin Syndrome versus NMS
steps.tx: **Differential diagnosis of hyperthermic syndromes** relies on rigorous examination of neuromuscular reflexes: serotonin syndrome uniquely displays neuromuscular hyperreactivity with spontaneous or inducible ocular clonus, generalized hyperreflexia, and shivering, predominantly affecting the lower extremities. Conversely, neuroleptic malignant syndrome presents with generalized hyporeflexia, lead-pipe rigidity, and a slow, insidious onset over days rather than hours.

right.title: NMS Hallmark
points: lead-pipe generalized rigidity, hyporeflexia, normal pupil size, and constipation

steps.title: Serotonin Syndrome Treatment
steps.tx: **Management of severe serotonin toxicity** requires immediate cessation of all serotonergic agents, supportive hydration, external cooling, and intravenous benzodiazepines to diminish muscular agitation and autonomic instability. For moderate to severe cases unresponsive to supportive care, the specific 5-HT2A receptor antagonist cyproheptadine is administered orally or crushed through a nasogastric tube.

steps.title: Mirtazapine Pharmacology
steps.tx: **Presynaptic alpha-2 antagonism by mirtazapine** disinhibits both serotonin and norepinephrine release without inhibiting monoamine reuptake transporters. By selectively antagonizing 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors, mirtazapine completely avoids antidepressant-induced nausea and sexual dysfunction. Its potent blockade of histamine H1 receptors produces prominent drowsiness and marked appetite stimulation, making it an outstanding choice for depressed patients with insomnia and anorexia.

steps.title: Bupropion Contraindications
steps.tx: **Bupropion mechanism and seizure hazard** involves dual norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibition (NDRI) without direct serotonergic activity, entirely sparing patients from sexual side effects while facilitating tobacco smoking cessation. However, bupropion significantly lowers seizure thresholds in a dose-dependent fashion, making it strictly contraindicated in patients with anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, or pre-existing seizure disorders.

steps.title: Trazodone and Priapism
steps.tx: **Serotonin modulator trazodone toxicity** centers on its combined 5-HT2A receptor antagonism, weak 5-HT reuptake inhibition, and potent alpha-1 adrenergic receptor blockade. Low doses (50 to 100 milligrams) are widely prescribed off-label for severe insomnia. However, alpha-1 adrenergic antagonism can impair sympathetic venous outflow from the corpora cavernosa, resulting in priapism, a painful urologic emergency requiring intracavernosal phenylephrine.
